prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

You are reviewing layouts of one table, all rendered in a real browser with identical content, font, padding and colours; only column widths differ. You do not know who or what produced them. The first image is the content overview (every cell on one line).
Table: 高一学生期中期末成绩汇总 (language zh-CN).
Grid: 8 columns × 8 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Merged cells: "姓名" spans 1 col × 2 row; "语文" spans 2 col × 1 row; "数学" spans 2 col × 1 row; "英语" spans 2 col × 1 row; "总分" spans 1 col × 2 row.
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "姓名" · longest unbreakable word 16px · one-line width 46px
  col 2: header "语文 › 期中" · longest unbreakable word 19px · one-line width 31px
  col 3: header "语文 › 期末" · longest unbreakable word 19px · one-line width 31px
  col 4: header "数学 › 期中" · longest unbreakable word 19px · one-line width 31px
  col 5: header "数学 › 期末" · longest unbreakable word 19px · one-line width 31px
  col 6: header "英语 › 期中" · longest unbreakable word 19px · one-line width 31px
  col 7: header "英语 › 期末" · longest unbreakable word 19px · one-line width 31px
  col 8: header "总分" · longest unbreakable word 28px · one-line width 31px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 360px (the dashed pink box = the reader's viewport). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 359px.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Rate EACH layout independently: "excellent" | "good" | "acceptable" | "poor" | "bad", with a short reason that points at what you see. Then name the best layout(s) (ties allowed), say how confident you are (low/medium/high), and note anything you are unsure about.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"ratings":{"A":{"grade":"","why":""},"B":{"grade":"","why":""},"C":{"grade":"","why":""},"D":{"grade":"","why":""}},"best":["letter"],"confidence":"","unsure":""}

log.raw: {"ratings":{"A":{"grade":"bad","why":"Names break into three lines and total scores split across lines, making both student identification and comparison difficult."},"B":{"grade":"acceptable","why":"Scores and totals remain intact, but names wrap across two lines and the exam-period headers stack vertically."},"C":{"grade":"poor","why":"Totals remain intact, but names stack one character per line, making rows unnecessarily tall and student identification harder."},"D":{"grade":"good","why":"Names, scores and totals stay intact, with compact rows and balanced subject pairs; the exam-period headers still wrap onto two lines."}},"best":["D"],"confidence":"high","unsure":"The exam-period headers wrap in every option shown; the ratings reflect the visible layouts rather than an unshown width allocation."}
